accepted.s: Which institution conducts the Census of India?
o: Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
accepted.x: The Census of India is conducted by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority responsible for the function rather than the ministry associated with statistics generally.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, synchronous census, delay, caste

accepted.s: The Census of India conducted in 2011 was the:
accepted.x: The 2011 Census was the 15th Census of India and the 7th Census conducted after Independence.
accepted.tq: Separate the total sequence number from the number counted after Independence.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, synchronous census, delay, caste

accepted.s: What was the motto of Census 2011?
accepted.x: The motto of Census 2011 was “Our Census, Our Future”.
accepted.tq: Test the exact official phrase and avoid substituting a familiar development slogan.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, synchronous census, delay, caste

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Census of India:
1. The first census in India was non-synchronous.
2. The first regular synchronous census was conducted in 1881.
3. The Census of India is conducted by the Election Commission of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The first census was non-synchronous and the first regular synchronous census was held in 1881. Statement 3 is false because the Census is conducted by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong authority statement after confirming the two historical statements.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, synchronous census, delay, caste

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between Census 2011 and Census 2027?
o: Census 2027 will come 16 years after Census 2011 because the 2021 Census was delayed
Census 2027 will be held 12 years after Census 2011
Census 2027 will be held 10 years after Census 2011
Census 2027 will be the first Census conducted after Independence
accepted.x: The 2021 Census was delayed, making Census 2027 the next Census and placing it 16 years after the 2011 Census.
accepted.tq: Use the interval and the intervening delay to eliminate familiar decennial assumptions.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, synchronous census, delay, caste

accepted.s: Census 2027 is significant because it is scheduled to include:
o: A Census confined to urban areas
Caste enumeration along with the population Census
Only economic-caste data and no population enumeration
accepted.x: Census 2027 is scheduled to include caste enumeration along with the population Census.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the defining new component from unrelated survey activities.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, synchronous census, delay, caste

accepted.s:
With regard to Census 2027, consider the following statements:
1. House listing is scheduled to continue up to 30 September 2026.
2. Population enumeration in snow-bound areas is scheduled for September 2026.
3. Population enumeration in other areas is scheduled for February 2027.
4. The enumeration is scheduled to be completed on 1 March 2027.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly state the notified schedule for house listing, enumeration in snow-bound and other areas, and completion on 1 March 2027.
accepted.tq: Check each date independently before selecting the comprehensive code.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, synchronous census, delay, caste

accepted.s: How many questions were notified for Census 2027, and how many of them were new?
accepted.x: Forty questions were notified for Census 2027, of which thirteen were new.
accepted.tq: Keep the total number and the subset number distinct when reading paired figures.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, synchronous census, delay, caste

accepted.s: Which of the following is cited as an example of a new question proposed for Census 2027?
accepted.x: Digital literacy, along with bank accounts, is cited as an example of a new subject in Census 2027.
accepted.tq: Select the specifically mentioned new census subject rather than a general socioeconomic indicator.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, synchronous census, delay, caste

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a criterion for classification as a Census Town?
o: At least 50 per cent of the total workers engaged in manufacturing
At least 75 per cent of male workers engaged in non-farm work
Population density of at least 400 persons per square kilometre
accepted.x: The Census Town criteria are population of 5,000 or more, at least 75 per cent of male workers in non-farm work, and density of at least 400 persons per square kilometre. A 50 per cent manufacturing criterion is not included.
accepted.tq: Find the option that changes the occupational condition and introduces an unrelated threshold.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, synchronous census, delay, caste

accepted.s: The Census Town criteria used since 1981 are scheduled to be:
o: changed to a uniform 10,000 population criterion
accepted.x: The Census Town criteria have remained unchanged since 1981 and are to be retained for Census 2027.
accepted.tq: Test continuity over time rather than assuming that a forthcoming Census changes every criterion.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, synchronous census, delay, caste

accepted.s: India's urban population constituted approximately what proportion of the total population in 2011, according to the Census Town discussion?
accepted.x: Approximately 31 per cent of India's population was urban in 2011.
accepted.tq: Use the approximate figure directly and reject the tempting decade-spaced alternatives.
accepted.sec: Census history - first census, synchronous census, delay, caste

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the child sex ratio in India:
1. It was 976 in 1961.
2. It was 927 in 2001.
3. The provisional figure for 2011 was 914.
4. The India Year Book figure for 2011 was 919.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The reported series includes 976 in 1961, 927 in 2001, a provisional 2011 figure of 914, and an India Year Book figure of 919 for 2011.
accepted.tq: Retain both the provisional and subsequently cited figures instead of treating them as interchangeable.
accepted.sec: Child sex ratio (0-6) - national figure, trend, best/worst States

accepted.s: Which of the following represents the broad trend in India's child sex ratio during the period covered by the Census figures?
o: A decline up to 2001 followed by a return to 976 in 2011
A decline from 976 in 1961 to the 2011 figures of 914/919
accepted.x: The child sex ratio declined from 976 in 1961 to 927 in 2001 and to the reported 2011 figures of 914 provisionally or 919 in the India Year Book.
accepted.tq: Compare the first and last values before considering the intermediate movement.
accepted.sec: Child sex ratio (0-6) - national figure, trend, best/worst States

accepted.s: The share of children in India's population declined from approximately 16 per cent in 2001 to:
accepted.x: The share of children declined from 16 per cent in 2001 to 13.1 per cent in 2011.
accepted.tq: Subtracting the two stated shares helps distinguish the precise percentage from nearby rounded values.
accepted.sec: Child sex ratio (0-6) - national figure, trend, best/worst States

accepted.s: What was notable about the child population in the 2011 Census?
o: It was the first census to record children as more than one-fourth of the population
It excluded the 0–6 age group from enumeration
It was the first census in decades to show fewer children in absolute numbers
It showed a rise in the child share to 16 per cent
accepted.x: The 2011 Census was the first census in decades to show a fall in the absolute number of children.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an absolute-number change from a percentage-share change.
accepted.sec: Child sex ratio (0-6) - national figure, trend, best/worst States

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (State)
a. Haryana
b. Punjab
c. Mizoram
d. Meghalaya
List-II (Child sex-ratio description)
i. 846
 ii. About 970
 iii. 834
 iv. About 970
accepted.x: Haryana had 834, Punjab 846, and Mizoram and Meghalaya had child sex ratios of about 970. The two best States therefore receive the two approximately 970 descriptions.
accepted.tq: Start with the two exact figures and then place the two approximately equal values.
accepted.sec: Child sex ratio (0-6) - national figure, trend, best/worst States

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Haryana had a lower child sex ratio than Punjab in 2011.
Reason (R): Haryana recorded a child sex ratio of 834, while Punjab recorded 846.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and the figures 834 and 846 directly explain why Haryana's child sex ratio was lower than Punjab's.
accepted.tq: Check whether the numerical reason directly establishes the comparison in the assertion.
accepted.sec: Child sex ratio (0-6) - national figure, trend, best/worst States

accepted.s: Which State is associated with the best child sex ratio among the States cited in the 2011 Census discussion?
accepted.x: Mizoram and Meghalaya were cited as having the best child sex ratios, at about 970; Mizoram is the matching State among the options.
accepted.tq: Identify the best-performing group while excluding the two specifically cited worst performers.
accepted.sec: Child sex ratio (0-6) - national figure, trend, best/worst States

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the child sex-ratio pattern cited for 2011?
o: Both Haryana and Punjab had about 970
accepted.x: The cited 2011 child sex ratios were 834 for Haryana and 846 for Punjab, while Mizoram and Meghalaya were the best-performing States at about 970.
accepted.tq: Directly discriminate between two neighbouring State figures that are easily interchanged.
accepted.sec: Child sex ratio (0-6) - national figure, trend, best/worst States

accepted.s: The sex ratio at birth reported under the Civil Registration System for 2024 was:
accepted.x: The Civil Registration System reported a sex ratio at birth of 917 for 2024.
accepted.tq: Read the current-affairs figure precisely and avoid shifting the final digit by ten.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following is associated with the current demographic policy discussion?
o: A High-Level Committee on Demographic Changes surveying States
A committee replacing the Registrar General with the Election Commission
A committee exclusively examining monsoon rainfall
accepted.x: A High-Level Committee on Demographic Changes is surveying States as part of the current demographic discussion.
accepted.tq: Match the committee's subject with the demographic issue rather than an unrelated public-policy field.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Delimitation Bill 2026 is reported to propose the use of which population data?
accepted.x: The Delimitation Bill 2026 is reported to propose using 2011 Census data.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific census base year instead of assuming that the latest scheduled Census must be used.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which concern has been raised regarding the Census Town definition?
accepted.x: The Census Town definition has been criticised on the ground that it may undercount the extent of urbanisation.
accepted.tq: Connect the classification rule with its possible measurement bias.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh and India:
1. Andhra Pradesh has a sex ratio of 997.
2. India's sex ratio is 943.
3. Andhra Pradesh's literacy rate is 67.35 per cent.
4. India's literacy rate is 72.98 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four figures are stated values: Andhra Pradesh has a sex ratio of 997 and literacy of 67.35 per cent, while India's corresponding figures are 943 and 72.98 per cent.
accepted.tq: Verify each State–national figure pair before using the comparison.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares Andhra Pradesh with India on the two indicators cited?
o: Andhra Pradesh is below India in both sex ratio and literacy
Andhra Pradesh is above India in sex ratio but below India in literacy
Andhra Pradesh is above India in both sex ratio and literacy
Andhra Pradesh is below India in sex ratio but above India in literacy
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh's sex ratio of 997 is higher than India's 943, whereas its literacy rate of 67.35 per cent is lower than India's 72.98 per cent.
accepted.tq: Compare the direction of difference separately for each indicator.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which State was the only State to record negative population growth during 2001–2011?
accepted.x: Nagaland was the only State recorded as having negative population growth during 2001–2011.
accepted.tq: Use the “only State” clue carefully because it identifies an exception rather than a general trend.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which statement about the status of Census 2011 is correct?
o: It is the latest published Census and the last one published so far
It was followed by a published Census in 2021
It was the first Census after Independence
accepted.x: The 2011 Census is the last Census published so far; the 2021 Census was delayed.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the last published Census from the next scheduled Census.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
